correctness.rationale: PASS. For each k>=3 each radius-(k-i) cycle ball is an arc of length 2(k-i)+1; the sum is k^2. A cover of order k^2 is disjoint, and a cover of order k^2-1 has a unique vertex of multiplicity two. The source-separation inequalities follow from pairwise arc nonoverlap or one-point endpoint overlap, including the last singleton. The proof uniquely encodes such one-short covers by a labelled cyclic order, overlap boundary, and cycle translation, and proves that precisely two valid one-coordinate slides move the overlap clockwise/counterclockwise. After k clockwise moves every arc has shifted one vertex; orbit length kn yields one C_kn for each of (k-1)! orders. The k=2 case is separately checked. Independent C++17 complete enumeration for k=2..5 and Python for k=2..4 reconstruct states/edges/components, supporting but not replacing the infinite proof. The code and actual output are embedded.

value.rationale: PASS. Adjacent movement of time-indexed optimal ignition sources is a natural graph-burning mobility question: it preserves the two true constraints of the process, unlike permutation-only scheduling. There is a sharp, structural single-vertex threshold at the burning-capacity square: the entire mobility graph changes from isolated states to long cyclic components generated by a unique movable overlap. Full graph isomorphism, component count and sharp component diameter for infinitely many cycles go beyond previously known burning number and provide a motivated benchmark for constrained source relocation.
